description: Step-02 salience scoring tag-list parser used regex `^\s+-\s+(.+)` which required at least one whitespace character before the list item dash. Most episodic frontmatter stores tags as unindented YAML block lists (`- tag` at column 0), so the parser returned an empty tag list for 119 of 122 files. Result: files_with_tags=3, in_window_count=3, score_distribution=0:119,1:2,2:1 — effectively zero co-occurrence signal. The same bug likely shaped prior-run distributions because dream-cycle reports listed heavy-tail at score-10 with no investigation. Caught when the v1 step-02 run looked wrong against prior log entries; fixed inline by changing the regex to `^\s*-\s+(.+)`. After fix: files_with_tags=117, in_window_count=58, distribution 0:12,2:3,6:2,7:8,9:6,10:91.
what_was_expected: Tag parser accepts both `- tag` (column 0) and `  - tag` (indented) block list formats per YAML spec.
what_happened: Parser only accepted indented list items; rejected the canonical layout used in the bulk of episodic memory; produced a near-zero score distribution that masked the issue.
proposed_fix: Permanently update the step-02 reference parser (and any future re-implementations) to use `^\s*-\s+(.+)` for block-list items. Add a sanity assertion: if files_with_tags < 50% of episodic_scanned and episodic_scanned > 20, surface a warning to the dream log because that ratio indicates a parser failure rather than corpus state.
